title: The French New Wave
subject: art
description: Young critics from *Cinema notebooks* go behind the camera. Between **1959** and **1968**, the New Wave freed film from the studio and invented modern auteur cinema.

hero.hook: Film critics steal cameras and reinvent the seventh art.

blocks.text: The **New Wave** (1959-1968) is not a simple style. It’s a power grab. Young French film buffs judge studio cinema to be too fixed, too polished, too written in advance. They want to film the way you write a novel: freely, in the first person.
By moving from criticism to production, they make the director the real author of the film. And they are changing world cinema.

Before the sets, there is a magazine: the **Cinema notebooks**, founded in **1951** by . Around him, young critics: **Jean-Luc Godard**, **François Truffaut**, **Claude Chabrol**, **Jacques Rivette**, **Éric Rohmer**. Their central idea is called the . [[André Bazin]] [[Author policy]]

blocks.caption: Les Cahiers du cinéma: the school where the New Wave learned to think about film.

blocks.text: For them, the real creator is not the screenwriter, but the one who directs. The framing, the rhythm, the cuts: these are the signature of an author, like the style of a novelist.

sections.title: 1959: Truffaut and Godard enter the scene

blocks.text: In **1959**, *The Four Hundred Blows* by **François Truffaut** triumphed in Cannes. The film follows **Antoine Doinel**, a teenage breakup, played by . The camera follows life rather than a strict scenario. The final look towards us crosses the : the hero looks at the audience, without a happy ending. [[Jean-Pierre Léaud]] [[fourth wall]]

blocks.caption: Antoine Doinel facing the sea: a youth who refuses a clear-cut destiny.

blocks.text: The following year, *Out of breath* by Godard, with , shocked with its abrupt cuts. Godard cuts in the middle of the gestures, as if he were writing with scissors. [[Jean-Paul Belmondo]]
These two films prove that we can tell stories differently: faster, freer, closer to the street.

The break is also technical.  cameras and more sensitive films allow . No more heavy studios: we film in cafes, apartments, and the streets of Paris, often in natural light. [[Éclair Caméflex]] [[Filming in natural settings and the light camera]]

The actors improvise. Speech becomes familiar, sometimes stuttering. Cinema breathes like life. This freedom then inspired the  in Brazil, then ultra-strict rules like the  in Denmark, distant heirs of the same thirst for authenticity. [[Cinema Novo]] [[Dogme 95]]

In the years **1970**, the **New Hollywood** was inspired by it: **Martin Scorsese**, **Francis Ford Coppola**, **Steven Spielberg** mix American efficiency and French freedom. The New Wave imposed a lasting idea: a film can carry the voice of a single person.

events.title: The Four Hundred Blows
events.detail: Truffaut imposes auteur cinema in Cannes.

blocks.text: The New Wave took cinema out of the studio and into the streets. It made the director an auteur, and this idea continues to shape independent cinema around the world.
